transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-20
Start Time (UTC): 15:30
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Morales, Priya Nair, Marcus Lee (Redwood); Aisha Rahman, Daniel Ortiz, Marta Kovac, Ravi Shah (Horizon Edge)

00:00 Ethan: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, hows it going?
00:06 Aisha: good thanks, excited to get this scoped, we want to be clear on timeline and what success looks like, we've got execs breathing down to see numbers in 6 weeks so we gotta be realistic
00:18 Ethan: totally, that is the plan to map a milestone cadence so you can take a confident exec readout at the end. I'll hand to Priya for the bench/ops details, but first quick context, what's the workload you want to evaluate?
00:27 Daniel: so it's primarily a user-facing extraction pipeline, average request size is 350 tokens, p95 is around 800 tokens when users paste long docs. Throughput target is about 40 rps sustained for peak, but average is closer to 8 rps. We also have a batch job that does nightly summarization, heavy on context window, up to 6k tokens.
00:47 Priya: right got it, so mix of interactive low-latency and high-context batch. For the POC we should test two profiles: steady-state interactive with concurrency shaping, and a batch run to validate memory/kv cache behavior.
01:03 Marcus: quick Q, when you say 40 rps peak what's the concurrency and latencies you want to guard? p95 p99 targets?
01:09 Daniel: p95 < 400ms, p99 < 900ms for the interactive path. For batch, throughput is less time-sensitive, but we want to measure token/sec and cost per 1k tokens.
01:20 Ethan: ok those are helpful. One thing to call out — if you run hosted it's easiest to spin up, but if you need strict data residency/VPC and KMS we'll recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private. Marta, I know security is key, do you have constraints?
01:33 Marta: yes, we need VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, SOC2 attestation, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also need a pattern for creds rotation and RBAC. We'll need to see architectural docs and certs.
01:46 Priya: absolutely, we can provide the SOC2 letter and an architecture diagram. Note that in Dedicated mode we can integrate with your KMS and deliver audit logs. For the POC sandbox we usually grant temporally-scoped credentials and a VPC tunnel.
01:57 Travis: 
01:58 Ethan: (laughs) that's Speaker 6, ignore him, ok next the milestone map. We propose 6 weeks: week 0 kickoff/access; weeks 1-2 baseline benching + model selection and quant profiles; week 3 mid-point review; weeks 4-5 optimizations and re-bench; week 6 exec readout. Thoughts?
02:17 Ravi: that aligns. Could the mid-point be earlier at week 2 to buy more iteration? Exec is non-negotiable at week 6.
02:25 Priya: we can do midpoint at week 2 if you prefer — initial baseline and smoke tests in first 10 business days then mid-review. The idea is to have a go/no-go gate defined by success criteria.
02:37 Ethan: let's define success criteria now. Suggested set: functional correctness on sample evals (F1/precision recall thresholds), latency SLOs: p95 < 400ms, p99 < 900ms for interactive, budgeted cost per 1k tokens not exceed X (we'll propose a target), and stability under 24h soak at average load. Also access & security checks passed.
02:56 Daniel: for correctness we'll give you a 300-example eval set and we want less than 3% regression from our current model.
03:06 Marcus: important detail — is the current baseline an internal model or a cloud vendor?
03:09 Daniel: internal, hybrid stack. We're open to mixed routing if that helps latency/cost.
03:15 Priya: ok for benchmarking we'll need: (1) sample prompt corpus, (2) request trace (timestamps, tokens), (3) representative concurrency profile. Daniel, can you export 48 hours of anonymized traces?
03:27 Daniel: yes, I'll work with infra to pull those. We need guidance on anonymization.
03:31 Marta: we also need to ensure no PII leaves our systems; we'll anonymize and mask as needed and host in a customer S3 bucket.
03:38 Ethan: perfect. For the actual runner we recommend our k6-based harness plus a small wrapper that hits either hosted or a dedicated endpoint. Priya will share the runner and a sample config.
03:48 Priya: sending that after the call. We'll include sample scaling parameters, concurrency, token distribution.
03:54 Aisha: on access, what's the fastest path: hosted sandbox or dedicated demo infra?
03:58 Priya: fastest = hosted, you get an endpoint in minutes. However, given KMS and VPC needs you'll probably want Dedicated for fidelity. For the POC we can spin a temporary Dedicated sandbox with restricted capacity which mimics production and supports KMS. That usually takes 3–5 business days to provision with our infra team.
04:16 Daniel: is there any risk that Dedicated performance differs from hosted?
04:19 Marcus: they should be similar; Dedicated uses same runtime and kernels, but you can pick instance types. We log kernel-level perf and can replicate production sizing. There are small variance factors like noisy neighbor — which is why we provision dedicated nodes for the POC.
04:31 Marta: okay confirm KMS integration on dedicated, we cannot accept keys leaving our tenancy.
04:35 Priya: confirmed, customer-managed KMS is supported, keys never leave customer KMS; Redwood stores only wrapped key metadata. We'll include an integration playbook.
04:45 Ethan: on benchmarks, two threads: perf (latency, throughput) and quality (output correctness/regression). We'll run baseline against your traces and then apply optimizations — batching, kv cache, quantization profiles — and re-run.
04:58 Daniel: quantization is a no-go for some of our evals due to small accuracy delta. Can you show quantization-by-slice?
05:05 Priya: yes we can do model variant testing: full float, 8-bit, and mixed quant profiles. We'll measure delta on eval set and include a per-slice breakdown. We also do prefix/KV cache tests to show cold vs warm latency.
05:17 Ravi: how will cost be measured? Tokenized cost per 1k and infra charges?
05:22 Marcus: we'll provide a cost report with per-token runtime cost and estimated infra amortized cost. For Dedicated we can show burn rate for the provisioned pool and effective cost per 1M tokens.
05:33 Aisha: ok sounds solid. For the mid-point we want a synthetic run that mirrors peak traffic for a 2-hour window — this is an exec-level risk test. Can that be scheduled in week 2?
05:44 Priya: yes we'll plan a 2-hour soak simulating peak concurrency. We'll run that in a staging window and capture p50/p95/p99, memory, GPU utilization, and eviction events.
05:56 Daniel: about data egress — we need to know what logs Redwood stores and the retention policy during the POC.
06:02 Ethan: we'll share our retention and telemetry matrix. By default logs are kept for 30 days in the sandbox and we can extend or purge on request. We also offer an option to stream logs to your SIEM so nothing lingers in Redwood.
06:13 Marta: good, please include the SIEM connector docs.
06:17 Marcus: noted.
06:20 Ethan: ok gating rules — propose three gates: Gate 1 (access & smoke): successful access to Dedicated sandbox and a passing smoke test within 5 days; Gate 2 (baseline bench): baseline run with metrics captured and no critical regressions at midpoint (week 2); Gate 3 (exec-readout): final run demonstrating target SLOs and cost/quality thresholds.
06:40 Ravi: do we need legal/contract sign-off before Dedicated provisioning?
06:43 Ethan: for full Dedicated reserved capacity yes, but for a sandbox we can spin temporary capacity under our standard POC MSA which is lightweight; we'll share the POC addendum. Legal team typically signs within 48–72 hours for sandbox.
06:58 Aisha: timeline sounds good. Let's lock the dates: kickoff/access week of 2027-05-24; baseline runs 5/31–6/6; midpoint review week of 6/7; iterate 6/8–6/20; exec readout week of 6/21. Is that feasible?
07:20 Priya: yes that maps to a 4-week active bench window plus a week each side — total 6 weeks. We'll send a calendar invite with proposed times.
07:27 Daniel: who from Redwood will run the benchmarks? We want the SE pair in the room during soak tests.
07:32 Priya: Marcus and I will be hands on for the soak and perf nights. We'll also provide the runner so your infra can re-run locally.
07:40 Marta: on compliance Q — will you sign an NDA that covers PII handling during the trace exchange?
07:44 Ethan: yes we'll send an NDA template and we can append a PII handling addendum. We'll also provide a checklist for data anonymization.
07:53 Daniel: small nit — sometimes transcripts and tokens differ; what's your tokenizer and how will you tokenize our payloads for fair apples-to-apples?
07:59 Marcus: we use the BPE-style tokenizer aligned with the model family; we'll share tokenizer scripts so you can token-count locally. We'll also report tokens in both raw and normalized forms.
08:09 Aisha: ok great. Any known blockers?
08:12 Priya: potential lead time is Dedicated sandbox provisioning and legal sign-off; otherwise the rest is operational. Also we need the traces and evaluation set by May 24 to hit the baseline window.
08:22 Ethan: action items recap and owners: I'll send the onboarding guide and checklist; Priya will send runner + benchmark plan; Daniel will share traces and eval set; Marta will push SOC2 and compliance Qs. We'll tentatively lock midpoint 2027-06-07 for review.
08:39 Ravi: yep that's fine. Also please include an example exec readout deck template so we can align messaging.
08:45 Ethan: will do.
08:47 Aisha: last question: if performance looks off after optimization, what are the typical next options?
08:52 Priya: we have a few levers: tweak batching, adjust kv cache sizing, try a different model variant or slightly larger instance type, or hybrid routing for hot requests. We'll document each tradeoff and estimated cost impact.
09:06 Daniel: ok thanks all.
09:08 Ethan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.
09:12 (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker label noise; some acronyms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "K V cash" instead of "KV cache"), minor word swaps.
